conviction_note: A mild long lean, p_up 57 on an abs move of 15 (implied 13.5%, median own reaction 16.6%, and the release carries the first FY27 quarter guide). Since Sanmina last spoke, AMD said on 2026-11-03 that Helios racks shipped for revenue in the September quarter, with a 'big step up' in Q4. Sanmina had said its next-gen accelerated-compute program was kept out of Q4 for revenue-recognition timing and ramps in fiscal Q1 2027, yet Q1 consensus revenue ($3.55bn) is only ~3% above the Q4 guide midpoint. The 38% one-month drawdown has a sector/political cause: yields on 2026-10-08, and the 2026-11-05 AI-hardware selloff after the midterms. It did not come from estimate cuts. Peers that printed into the same washout (CLS, FLEX) jumped on beat-and-raise. Against that: Sanmina's own Helios role is inferred from press and not confirmed, legacy ZT programs and memory shortages cut against a clean ramp, the stock bounced ~9% intraday today before the seal, and skew is mildly put-bid. That is why p_up sits at 57, not higher. The findings sum (+3.0) is a little above the scaled number (+2.1) because the scaled number carries the sign uncertainty and the findings do not.
bar: Q4 FY26 (quarter ended 2026-10-03): company guide revenue $3.3-3.6bn, non-GAAP EPS $3.05-3.35, non-GAAP op margin 7.5-8.0% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000897723/000089772326000036/sanmina_exx991xjune272026.htm). Consensus per Yahoo (4 analysts): revenue $3.48bn (3.45-3.54), EPS $3.27 (3.21-3.35), flat over 90 days. Next quarter (Q1 FY27, Dec 2026): revenue $3.55bn (3.38-3.70), EPS $2.95 (2.51-3.52). FY27: revenue $16.70bn, EPS $14.08 (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SANM/analysis/). MarketBeat cites $3.5bn Q4 revenue consensus. Earnings Whispers' $3.63bn / $2.90 is a pre-guide figure and is not used. Management said in July it is confident in >$16bn FY27 revenue, H2-weighted, with no formal FY27 guide.

findings.finding: AMD (direct counterparty; Sanmina bought ZT Systems' manufacturing from AMD) said on its 2026-11-03 Q3 call that the September quarter 'was the first quarter that we shipped MI455X Helios racks for revenue', that 'we have a big step up in Q4', that data center revenue grows ~50% sequentially in Q4, and that 2027 revenue grows >80%. Sanmina had told investors on 2026-07-27 that its next-gen accelerated-compute program was excluded from the Q4 outlook for revenue-recognition timing and ramps from fiscal Q1 2027 (Oct-Dec 2026). Yet Q1 FY27 consensus revenue is $3.55bn, only ~3% above the $3.45bn Q4 guide midpoint, and FY27 consensus is $16.7bn against management's '>$16bn'. A Q1 guide carrying the rack ramp would clear that bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock trades on. 2026-07-27: -17.46% on a Q4 revenue guide midpoint ~2% under consensus, despite an EPS beat ($3.31 vs $2.77). 2026-01-26: -21.56% on a tepid guide. 2026-04-27: +14.56% on beat, raised FY26 and a $600m buyback. 2025-11-03: +16.56% on a Q1 guide above estimates.
findings.why_not_priced: Had the market priced a Helios-driven step-up, Q1 FY27 consensus would have moved up after AMD's 2026-11-03 call. Instead Yahoo shows no estimate change in 7-30 days, and the stock fell ~15% in the week AMD rose ~7%, pulled down by a sector-wide political selloff. Sanmina's own exposure to Helios is not confirmed by either company, so sell-side has not modelled it into the quarter.
findings.independence: Sanmina's own July guidance commentary (next-gen program excluded from Q4 for rev-rec timing, ramps fiscal Q1 2027; >$16bn FY27): https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/sanmina-q3-earnings-call-highlights (via search snippet). The Next Platform names Sanmina/ZT as the likely Helios NPI manufacturing partner: https://www.nextplatform.com/2026/02/23/amd-says-helios-racks-and-mi400-series-gpus-on-track-for-2h-2026/. AMD Q4 guide of ~$17bn: https://www.xtb.com/en/market-analysis/amd-shares-jump-7-after-stellar-earnings-will-semiconductor-stocks-return-to-growth. All of these are AMD-side or press. Sanmina's share of Helios is an inference: Celestica builds the Helios scale-up switches, not racks (https://www.amd.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-3-16-amd-and-celestica-announce-collaboration-to-a.html), and AMD names HPE/Dell/Lenovo/Supermicro as system shippers. AMD also guided Q4 gross margin down on low-margin early Helios systems, which may dilute Sanmina's margin percentage on the ramp. Sized net of the legacy/memory offset filed separately.

findings.finding: Sanmina's 2026-07-27 call said ZT Systems' Q4 outlook ($0.8-1.0bn of the $3.3-3.6bn) was cut below prior implied guidance on timing of 'a few legacy programs', with legacy accelerated compute described as close to zero. CEO Sola flagged material shortages (memory, custom ASICs) that could persist into 2027. Both can hold the Q1 FY27 guide below what the new program alone implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time ZT timing slipped (2026-07-27 Q4 ZT guide below prior implied) the stock fell 17.46% the next session.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. It is public since July and was the cause of the -17% reaction, so most of it sits in consensus. What is not priced is whether legacy roll-off continues into Q1 against the new-program ramp: consensus Q1 revenue has a $3.38-3.70bn range, so the street disagrees on the net.
findings.independence: Same July call as finding 1's company-side source, read from the opposite side (two readings of one call, the legacy part versus the new-program part; sized as the offset net of finding 1). Memory shortage comment: https://statementdog.com/analysis/SANM/earnings_calls/317093 (search snippet). AMD separately said on 2026-11-03 'demand is higher than supply' and 'we have secured more supply'.

findings.finding: The 38% one-month fall (from ~$229 on 2026-10-02 to $134.91 at the 2026-11-06 close) has a sourced sector/political cause, not a company one. TipRanks 2026-10-08 attributes it to rising yields and oil. On 2026-11-05 an AI-hardware selloff after the Democratic midterm wins, including Texas' new governor promising a data-center moratorium, took CLS -13%, SMCI -10% and Dell -11%, with no company news. Over the same span SANM's current-quarter EPS estimate moved $3.26 to $3.27 over 90 days. Peers that printed into the same washout re-rated hard on beat-and-raise: Celestica, at a 52-week low on 2026-10-26, rose +12.1% and +8.4% on the next two sessions, and Flex rose +11.6% on 2026-10-28. SANM is +~9% intraday today (spot $146.83) before its print, so part of that relief is already taken.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SANM's reactions alternate: +16.56 (2025-11), -21.56 (2026-01), +14.56 (2026-04), -17.46 (2026-07). The April +14.56% came after a ~20% drawdown into the print, which is the closest analogue.
findings.why_not_priced: If the drawdown reflected company-specific disappointment, estimates would have been cut, and they were not (Yahoo revisions flat; StockStory 2026-11-07: 'analysts have generally reconfirmed their estimates'). The price, not the bar, moved. The cause (data-center policy risk) cannot be refuted by one print, though, and is a forward risk management may be asked about. Hence the small size.

Yields cause: https://www.tipranks.com/news/catalyst/sanmina-stock-slumps-as-rising-yields-spook-investors. This is a proxy (peer reactions), not a Sanmina number.

findings.finding: The reported quarter is likely inside the guide, with a bar slightly above its midpoint. Consensus is $3.48bn / EPS $3.27 against the guide midpoint of $3.45bn / $3.20. Counterparties that reported the same calendar quarter beat above their own ranges: Celestica revenue $5.83bn vs $5.40bn est, above the top of its guide; Flex FQ2 $8.5bn with EPS $1.18 vs ~$1.05; AMD Data Center $8.55bn vs $8.27bn. Sanmina beat EPS by $0.54 last quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats have been sold when the guide disappointed: 2026-07-27, an EPS beat of $3.31 vs $2.77 still closed -17.46%. 2026-01-26 (Q1 FY26) was a beat with a guide cut, -21.56%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It lands inside a range the company guided to, so the market was told to expect it. The only unpriced part is the peer read-through that the quarter's AI demand ran hot, worth a fraction of a point.

findings.finding: The working-capital build is large. Inventories were $3.15bn at 2026-06-27 against $1.99bn at FY25 end, Q3 free cash flow was only $24m (operating cash flow $124m), and total debt was ~$2.17bn against ~$0.3bn at FY25 end (ZT purchase). There was no buyback in Q3. Asked what the money buys: the inventory build lines up with a rack ramp that AMD has now confirmed is shipping, so this is a quality-of-print item more than a distress signal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Weiss (2026-09-01) cites the sharp FCF drop and no buybacks as reasons for post-Q3 weakness. Direct reaction to cash flow alone is not isolable in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced since July. What is open is whether Q4 cash conversion improves or inventory builds further ahead of the Q1 ramp. A further build with an explicit ramp is neutral; a build without one is negative.
findings.independence: https://weissratings.com/en/instant-news-alerts/sanmina-corporation-sanm-down-4-8-should-i-book-it-and-bail (2026-09-01) notes the FCF drop and no buybacks. AMD's confirmed Helios shipments are the ramp the build would fund (shares a source with finding 1).

findings.finding: The Eckert qui tam suit against subsidiary SCI Technology settled for $5.9m in total (agreement-in-principle May 2026, disclosed in the Q3 10-Q, no admission of liability). It is immaterial against ~$12 of FY26 EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction; the item has been disclosed since May.
findings.why_not_priced: Already disclosed and immaterial, so the price reflects it. It is filed only because Simply Wall St (2026-10-19) lists governance concerns from the settlement as a risk.

outside_window.finding: Texas data-center moratorium risk after the 2026-11 governor race (Texas holds >25% of planned US data-center capacity through 2030). A policy outcome dated well after the window; it can only reach this print through management commentary.
Anthropic's up-to-2GW MI450 deployment, first major phase H1 2027. This is FY27 H2-weighted demand that management said drives >$16bn FY27; it resolves after the window except through the guide.

baseline_tension: The lean is long while skew is mildly put-bid (+3.5 vol points). That is not a strong skew, call OI dominates (P/C 0.2), short interest is low, and the 20-day run-up (-31%) means the long lean cuts against a priced disappointment the estimates do not show. The ~9% intraday bounce today, before the seal, already takes part of the relief, which keeps p_up at 57.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5: the drawdown/peer-rebound finding is a proxy, not a Sanmina number, so it moved from +1.5 to +1.0. It was kept because the drawdown has a sourced cause and estimates were flat, unlike an unexplained drawdown, which the lesson sizes at 0.

Lesson 6: the reported-quarter finding lands inside the company's guided range, so it moved from +0.5 to +0.3. The bar is sourced to the guide plus Yahoo's 4-analyst consensus, and Earnings Whispers' stale figure is rejected.
Lesson 4: the working-capital/FCF item was treated as a financing question. The build corroborates a ramp AMD confirmed, so it moved from -0.5 to -0.3.

Lessons 1, 3 and 9 left the AMD guidance finding at +3.0: it lands on guidance, the line this name trades on, and is sized net of the legacy/memory offset, which stays a separate -1.0 with one sign each. p_up moved from 58 to 57 because the main finding's Sanmina link is inferred.
